High-frequency linear transducer (7.5–15 MHz) gray-scale and power/color Doppler sonography of the anterior, lateral, medial, and posterior compartments of the ankle and hindfoot performed in longitudinal and transverse planes with dynamic stress maneuvers as indicated.
FINDINGS:
ANTERIOR COMPARTMENT:
Tibiotalar Joint Recess: Normal physiological fluid (less than 3 mm). No significant joint effusion, hemarthrosis, or synovial hypertrophy.
Anterior Extensor Tendons (Tibialis Anterior, EHL, EDL): Normal uniform fibrillar echotexture and intact tendon sheaths without tenosynovitis or tear.
Anterior Inferior Tibiofibular Ligament (AITFL): Intact, continuous fibrillar band spanning the distal syndesmosis.
LATERAL COMPARTMENT:

Anterior Talofibular Ligament (ATFL): Continuous, taut fibrillar structure from the lateral malleolus to the talar neck without thickening, laxity, or disruption on dynamic anterior drawer/inversion stress.
Calcaneofibular Ligament (CFL): Intact deep fibrillar band beneath the peroneal tendons without tear or surrounding fluid.

Peroneal Tendons (Peroneus Longus & Brevis): Normal fibrillar echotexture, located normally within the retromalleolar groove with an intact superior peroneal retinaculum. No tenosynovitis, split tear, or dynamic subluxation.
MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Deltoid Ligament Complex: Intact superficial and deep fibers from the medial malleolus to the talus, calcaneus, and navicular without tear or edema.
Medial Flexor Tendons (Tibialis Posterior, FDL, FHL): Normal caliber and fibrillar architecture without tenosynovitis or tear.
Tarsal Tunnel: Tibial nerve and posterior tibial vessels are unremarkable without space-occupying ganglion cyst or varicosities.

Kager's Fat Pad & Retrocalcaneal Bursa: Normal homogeneous fat pad; retrocalcaneal bursa is collapsed (less than 2 mm) without fluid distension.
Plantar Fascia: Normal thickness at the calcaneal origin (___ mm; normal less than 4 mm) with preserved fibrillar echogenicity.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Mild generalized ankle discomfort; rule out effusion or tendinopathy.

subs.title: Findings
items: High-frequency sonographic evaluation of the anterior, lateral, medial, and posterior compartments of the right ankle demonstrates intact, normal fibrillar architecture of the Achilles tendon (4.8 mm AP thickness), tibialis anterior, peroneal, and medial flexor tendons without tenosynovitis or tear.
The anterior talofibular (ATFL), calcaneofibular (CFL), anterior inferior tibiofibular (AITFL), and deltoid ligaments are intact without thickening or dynamic instability.
The tibiotalar joint recess shows no significant effusion, and the plantar fascia is normal in thickness (3.1 mm).

subs.title: Impression
items: Normal right ankle ultrasound. No evidence of ligamentous injury, tendinopathy, tenosynovitis, or joint effusion.

bank.title: 2. Lateral Ankle Sprain — ATFL & CFL Tears (Traumatic)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Acute inversion injury to the left ankle 24 hours ago with severe lateral swelling and bruising.

subs.title: Findings
items: Anterior Talofibular Ligament (ATFL): Complete full-thickness disruption of the left ATFL at its fibular attachment, demonstrating wavy, retracted ligamentous ends separated by a 7 mm gap filled with hypoechoic hematoma/fluid. Dynamic gentle anterior drawer stress confirms abnormal talar translation and absence of ligamentous tension.
Calcaneofibular Ligament (CFL): The CFL is thickened (4.5 mm) and hypoechoic with partial-thickness interstitial tearing and surrounding periligamentous edema, though deep continuity is preserved.
Tibiotalar Joint: Small anechoic tibiotalar joint effusion with surrounding lateral subcutaneous soft tissue edema.

subs.title: Impression
items: Complete full-thickness tear (Grade III sprain) of the left anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL) with dynamic laxity.
Partial-thickness tear (Grade II sprain) of the left calcaneofibular ligament (CFL) and small reactive tibiotalar joint effusion.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Sudden "pop" in the posterior right lower leg during tennis with inability to plantarflex and positive Thompson test.

subs.title: Findings
items: Approximately 4.5 cm proximal to the calcaneal insertion (watershed zone), there is complete, full-thickness discontinuity of the right Achilles tendon fibers with frayed, retracted tendon stumps separated by a 2.8 cm gap in neutral position.
The tendon gap is filled with heterogeneous echogenic hematoma and herniated echogenic fat from Kager's fat pad.
Dynamic passive plantarflexion reduces the tendon gap to 0.9 cm with partial apposition of the torn ends.
The plantaris tendon remains intact medially.

subs.title: Impression
items: Complete full-thickness tear of the right mid-substance Achilles tendon, located 4.5 cm proximal to the calcaneal insertion, with a 2.8 cm retraction gap in neutral position (reducing to 0.9 cm in plantarflexion).
Urgent orthopedic surgical consultation recommended.

bank.title: 4. Peroneal Tendon Subluxation & Longitudinal Split Tear (Traumatic)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Lateral ankle snapping sensation and retromalleolar pain following a skiing injury.

subs.title: Findings
items: Dynamic Evaluation: With active dorsiflexion and eversion of the ankle, the peroneus brevis and peroneus longus tendons subluxate anteriorly out of the retromalleolar fibular groove over the lateral malleolus, associated with stripping and thickening of the superior peroneal retinaculum.

Tendon Morphology: The peroneus brevis tendon demonstrates a "boomerang/C-shaped" configuration with a focal longitudinal hypoechoic split cleft at the level of the distal fibula, accompanied by moderate anechoic fluid distending the common peroneal tendon sheath.

subs.title: Impression
items: Dynamic anterior subluxation of the peroneal tendons secondary to superior peroneal retinacular injury.
Longitudinal split tear of the peroneus brevis tendon with moderate peroneal tenosynovitis.

bank.title: 5. High Ankle Sprain (Syndesmotic / AITFL Tear - Traumatic)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: External rotation injury to the right ankle with pain proximal to the ankle joint line.

subs.title: Findings
items: Across the anterior distal tibiofibular syndesmosis, the anterior inferior tibiofibular ligament (AITFL) is completely disrupted with loss of normal fibrillar continuity, wavy retracted fibers, and localized hypoechoic fluid/hematoma.
Dynamic external rotation stress demonstrates abnormal widening of the distal tibiofibular clear space (measuring 6.8 mm vs. 3.5 mm on the asymptomatic left side).
The ATFL and deltoid ligaments are intact.

subs.title: Impression
items: Complete tear of the right anterior inferior tibiofibular ligament (AITFL) with dynamic syndesmotic widening, consistent with an unstable high ankle sprain.
Orthopedic evaluation and weight-bearing radiographs/CT advised to assess syndesmotic stability.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Chronic posterior heel pain and palpable mid-substance Achilles thickening in a distance runner.

subs.title: Findings
items: Achilles Tendon: Fusiform, asymmetric thickening of the mid-substance left Achilles tendon (measuring 11.5 mm in AP thickness) with ill-defined hypoechoic areas, loss of normal fibrillar architecture, and prominent intratendinous neovascularity (Grade 3 hyperemia) on power Doppler. No partial or full-thickness tear is identified.

Retrocalcaneal Bursa: Distended by a well-circumscribed, hypoechoic fluid collection measuring 1.4 x 0.6 cm between the anterior aspect of the distal Achilles tendon and the posterosuperior calcaneus, with mild surrounding hyperemia.

subs.title: Impression
items: Severe non-insertional left Achilles tendinopathy with active neovascularity on power Doppler; no tendon tear.
Retrocalcaneal bursitis.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Sharp medial plantar heel pain worst with the first steps in the morning.

subs.title: Findings
items: At its origin on the medial calcaneal tuberosity, the proximal right plantar fascia is markedly thickened (measuring 6.8 mm; normal less than 4.0 mm) and diffusely hypoechoic with loss of normal fibrillar striation and mild perifascial soft tissue edema.
Power Doppler demonstrates mild hyperemia at the calcaneal enthesis, with an underlying small plantar calcaneal spur.
No focal plantar fibroma or fascial rupture is present.

subs.title: Impression
items: Right proximal plantar fasciitis, evidenced by marked fascial thickening (6.8 mm), hypoechogenicity, and entheseal hyperemia.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Progressive medial ankle pain, swelling, and acquired flatfoot deformity.

subs.title: Findings
items: Posterior and inferior to the medial malleolus, the left tibialis posterior tendon is markedly enlarged (measuring 9.2 mm in diameter, greater than twice the caliber of the adjacent flexor digitorum longus tendon), heterogeneous, and hypoechoic with longitudinal intrasubstance splits.
The tendon sheath is markedly distended with complex anechoic/hypoechoic fluid and thickened hyperemic synovium on power Doppler.

subs.title: Impression
items: Severe left posterior tibial tendinopathy with longitudinal intrasubstance tearing and proliferative tenosynovitis (consistent with posterior tibial tendon dysfunction).

bank.title: 9. Tarsal Tunnel Ganglion Cyst & Sinus Tarsi / Anterior Ankle Ganglion (Non-Traumatic)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Palpable, fluctuating lump over the anterolateral ankle (or medial ankle paresthesias).

subs.title: Findings
items: Overlying the anterolateral tibiotalar joint line, superficial to the extensor tendons, there is a well-circumscribed, lobulated, multiseptated anechoic cystic mass measuring 2.2 x 1.4 x 0.9 cm with posterior acoustic enhancement, non-compressibility, and absence of internal Doppler vascularity.
A thin tortuous neck extends deeply toward the anterior tibiotalar joint capsule.
[Alternative for Tarsal Tunnel: Located within the medial tarsal tunnel immediately adjacent to the posterior tibial nerve, causing mild focal nerve displacement.]

subs.title: Impression
items: Lobulated anterolateral ankle ganglion cyst (2.2 cm) communicating with the tibiotalar joint capsule.
